{"artifact":"SmeDossierEnvelope","schema_version":"0.4.0","stage_id":"02.dossier_sections","probe":"rdmv-az-d","lineage":{"input_manifest_sha256":"51581099bd049ba733f838f5e2d3aed8378792ca9a5e9bc3c3a25fad9d47a78b","candidate_lineage_id":"2026-10-28-rdmv-az-class-d:lineage:33","source_registry_sha256":"6dbbc2d22fea619728bdb90038a4aedf3afc07eab652b3f97027c9c69aaadaf4","source_liveness_sha256":"1c5753487760cbe2044d84b5696121c7181af61815b598d89d5ce158abf5fe43"},"envelope_scope":{"kind":"partial_chunk","assigned_section_ids":["C2"],"chunk_index":1,"chunk_total":1},"section_char_limit":12000,"sections":[{"section_id":"C2","chunk_id":"C2.01","merge_seq":1,"domain":"Parking-distance, freeway-merge, gore-area and HOV confusables","heading":"C2 — Confusable pairs and knowledge-graph hints: the three parking distances, merging and exiting, missed exits, the right lane, gore areas, freeway stops and HOV lanes","learner_facing":false,"markdown":"## C2 — Confusable pairs and knowledge-graph hints: the three parking distances, merging and exiting, missed exits, the right lane, gore areas, freeway stops and HOV lanes
Look-alike numbers and rules from the parking and freeway pages, each tied to one handbook page; hint metadata sits only in the trailing line of a block.

FACT_ID: sec08-R01 | anchor: A01
The no-parking distances differ by object: 15 feet from a fire hydrant, 20 feet from a crosswalk at an intersection, and 50 feet from a railroad crossing. [A01]
Why it matters: group prohibited parking; difficulty three; confusable sec08-F09 versus sec08-F10.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0031]

FACT_ID: sec08-R02 | anchor: A01
Freeway parking is banned except for emergencies, and an emergency stop still calls for the shoulder, the brake, the engine off and warning signals. [A01]
Why it matters: group parking; difficulty two; confusable sec08-F07 versus sec08-F02.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0031]

FACT_ID: sec08-R03 | anchor: A01
On entry you match the speed of the freeway right lane, while on exit most freeways give you a deceleration lane in which to brake smoothly. [A01]
Why it matters: group merging; difficulty two; confusable sec08-F14 versus sec08-F17.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0031]

FACT_ID: sec08-R04 | anchor: A01
A solid line is off-limits both when entering and when exiting a freeway, and so is the gore area on entry. [A01]
Why it matters: group merging; difficulty two; prereq sec08-F15.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0031]

FACT_ID: sec08-R05 | anchor: A02
A missed exit is handled by driving on to the next exit and following signs back, never by stopping or reversing. [A02]
Why it matters: group exits; difficulty one; prereq sec08-F24.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0032]

FACT_ID: sec08-R06 | anchor: A02
The right lane of a highway with three or more lanes can carry traffic both slower and faster than the other lanes, because it serves entering and exiting vehicles. [A02]
Why it matters: group lane use; difficulty two; confusable sec08-F26 versus sec08-F25.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0032]

FACT_ID: sec08-R07 | anchor: A02
A gore area is the wedge between the through road and a ramp; driving over it and parking in it are both against the law. [A02]
Why it matters: group gore area; difficulty two; prereq sec08-F29.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0032]

FACT_ID: sec08-R08 | anchor: A02
By day you signal for freeway help with flashers or a raised hood, while after dark you add the dome light or flares and portable warning signals. [A02]
Why it matters: group freeway stops; difficulty two; prereq sec08-F31.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0032]

FACT_ID: sec08-R09 | anchor: A03
The HOV rule counts the driver as one of the two persons required, and it binds only at the posted weekday times. [A03]
Why it matters: group HOV; difficulty three; prereq sec08-F35.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0033]

FACT_ID: sec08-R10 | anchor: A03
Shoulder parking on a freeway is banned except in an emergency, while stopping is allowed only in areas specially provided. [A03]
Why it matters: group freeway restrictions; difficulty two; prereq sec08-F40.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0033]

FACT_ID: sec08-R11 | anchor: A03
On a three-lane highway the far right lane is treated as the slower through lane and the far left lane as the passing lane. [A03]
Why it matters: group lane use; difficulty two; prereq sec08-F43.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0033]

FACT_ID: sec08-R12 | anchor: A03
Car pools, motorcycles and buses may use an HOV lane during restricted times, and crossing its solid white line requires a signal. [A03]
Why it matters: group HOV; difficulty two; confusable sec08-F35 versus sec08-F37.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0033]
